standard_prerequisites.name: The passage from all m to pseudo-coherent

core_obligations: Use the decomposition of the diagonal triangle to get m-pseudo-coherence of a shifted sum of one summand with itself (proof lines 16205-16213).
Iterate to obtain m-pseudo-coherence of all shifts of the shifted summand (proof lines 16214-16217).
Apply the characterisation for large shifts (proof lines 16218-16219).
Work backwards along the triangles to conclude for the summand, and derive the pseudo-coherent case (proof lines 16220-16228).
proof_roadmap: Diagonal triangle and cone lemma (proof lines 16205-16213).
Large shifts and backwards induction (proof lines 16218-16226).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that if a direct sum of two complexes is m-pseudo-coherent then so is each summand. The proof uses the decomposition of the diagonal triangle for a direct sum into the sum of the two trivial triangles for the summands, so that the cone lemma produces m-pseudo-coherence of a shifted direct sum of one summand with itself; iterating gives m-pseudo-coherence of all successive shifts of that summand, and for large shifts the characterisation of m-pseudo-coherence makes the single shifted summand m-pseudo-coherent. Working backwards through the distinguished triangles relating consecutive shifts yields m-pseudo-coherence of the summand itself, and the pseudo-coherent case follows from the characterisation.
